So, Viviane, tell me about a project you are really proud of.
The Great Place to Work certification. It was my project from the first meeting to the last day.
Interesting. Where did you start?
At the beginning nobody believed in it. So first we ran a pilot in four stores.
Why only four stores?
Because I needed one number to show the board. The pilot gave me that number.
And after that?
After that we trained every store manager. Six months later we ran the survey in the whole company, and in the end we got the certification.
That is a strong story. Most candidates tell me what they are responsible for. You told me what changed.

I want to tell you about a project that almost died. Three years ago our turnover was thirty per cent and nobody in the company talked about culture. I asked for money for a culture project and the answer was no. So I changed the plan. First I ran a very small pilot in four stores, with no budget at all. It took us three months. The result was clear: in those four stores people stayed. That was the turning point. After that the finance director became my sponsor, because now I had a number and not an opinion. Six months later we trained every store manager, and in the end we ran the survey in the whole company. We got the certification in November. The project that nobody wanted is now the project everybody talks about.

Here is the mistake almost everybody makes. The recruiter asks about an achievement, and the candidate starts describing the company, the department, the history of the sector. Two minutes later the recruiter still does not know what the person did. So use this shape and nothing else. One: the problem before you arrived. Two: the two or three things you actually did, in order. Three: the result, with a number. Sixty seconds is enough. And please, do not use we for everything. If you led the project, say I led it. Brazilian candidates say we a lot, and it is polite, but the recruiter needs to hear what you did. Say we for the team and I for your decisions. That is not arrogance. That is information.
